newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir chief wants Pakistan to stop "proxy war".
newsitem.headline: Kashmir chief wants Pakistan to stop "proxy war".

text.p: The chief of India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state on Saturday urged Indian officials currently holding peace talks with Pakistan to tell their counterparts to stop a "proxy war" in Kashmir.
Top level Indian and Pakistani diplomats resumed a second round of peace talks on Friday in Islamabad.
The first round was held in March in New Delhi which was seen as a fresh start to bilateral negotiations that had broken down in 1994 due to differences over Kashmir.

"Pakistan has launched a proxy war in Kashmir, they will not succeed in this, I hope that the foreign secretary of India will take this issue with Pakistan," Farooq Abdullah, chief minister of Kashmir said at a police function at Zewan on the outskirts of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
Over a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir, India's only Moslem majority state.
India accuses Pakistan of arming and training separatist guerrillas but Pakistan says it only provides the separatists with political and diplomatic support.
"We want Pakistan-occupied Kashmir's return to us along with the northern territory," Abdullah said.
India rules two-thirds and Pakistan the rest of Kashmir, over which the two countries have fought two of their three wars since their independence from Britian in 1947.
"India is a peace loving country and wants peaceful solutions for all outstanding issues," he said

Abdullah blamed Pakistan for killing of about 50,000 Kashmiris during a seven-year-old rebellion in the Himalayan region. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people died since militancy erupted in the state in 1990.
